newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Thousands bid dead Nigerian musician Fela farewell.
newsitem.headline: Thousands bid dead Nigerian musician Fela farewell.

text.p: Several thousand people filed past the embalmed body of Fela Anikulapo-Kuti on Monday to say a last goodbye to the maverick Afrobeat musician who died of AIDS.

"Fela lives forever," said a banner fluttering in front of the platform on which was laid the corpse of the composer, singer and saxophonist who created the Afrobeat sound and popularised the continent's music across the globe.
The mood at Tafawa Balewa Square in the heart of Lagos was anything but sombre as fans danced to the sound of Fela's band, Egypt 80, which played a selection of old hits.
Anikulapo-Kuti, known to his fans simply as Fela, died of heart failure related to AIDS on August 2. He was 58.
Fela, a star of the Nigerian and international music scene in the 1970s and 1980s, won a reputation for smoking marijuana, sleeping with large numbers of women and dressing only in his underpants.
Fela's emaciated body, dressed in tight-fitting yellow trousers, multi-coloured shirt and black leather shoes, lay in a plain glass casket as people filed past under the tropical sun.
"We will all miss you Fela, we will all miss you, because you fought for social justice," said Bayo Martins, one of Nigeria's leading drummers, as he moved past.
Fela got under the skin of succesive military regimes with songs that portrayed soldiers as being below average intelligence.
He was detained on numerous occasions for a variety of offences and spent time in jail.

But for the last two years Fela did not publicly challenge current military strongman General Sani Abacha, even though his younger brother, activist Beko Ransome-Kuti is serving a prison sentence for allegedly taking part in a coup plot.

As the most well-known Nigerian to have died of AIDS, Fela has drawn attention to the spread of HIV infection, which causes the disease, through Africa's most populous nation of over 100 million people.
Fela is to be buried on Tuesday at his home in the working class Ikeja district.
